result.answer: Under RBI CCO guidelines, the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) in NBFC-Middle Layer and Upper Layer is subject to strict dual-hatting restrictions and must be appointed for a minimum fixed tenure of not less than 3 years. The CCO must not be assigned any business, commercial, or operational responsibilities that give rise to a conflict of interest.
result.legal_analysis: Under the RBI Circular on Compliance Function in NBFCs (April 11, 2022), the CCO must be a senior executive with independent reporting directly to the MD & CEO and/or the Audit Committee of the Board (ACB). Strict dual-hatting restrictions prohibit the CCO from holding any operational roles (e.g., credit, business origination, finance, audit). Furthermore, the CCO must have a minimum tenure of not less than 3 years to ensure independence, and premature removal or transfer requires prior approval of the Board of Directors with reporting to the Reserve Bank.

conditions_and_exceptions: In exceptional circumstances where temporary oversight is required, the CCO must not hold roles conflicting with compliance oversight.
Removal before completion of 3 years requires explicit Board resolution and immediate notification to the Department of Supervision, RBI.
material_assumptions: Applies to NBFCs classified under Middle Layer or Upper Layer.
